source: tools/collect_width200_loops.py over sequel-data/mirror/E0074/hatteras-<job>/out/step-*/summary.json and evidence/E0074/hatteras-<job>.json; width 100 from evidence/E0060-results.json. Supersedes evidence/E0074-interim.json (its two loops reproduce step for step, same sha256).
findings: Three of ten loops completed all 213 steps (f* 0.84, 0.74, 0.65), as at width 100 (E0060, every f* complete). The other seven were cancelled on Nov 26 at about 11:24Z (D0094) because each had passed the 100 CPU-hour per-run limit in budgets.yaml (101.13 to 101.15 CPU-hours by Slurm); the f* 0.65 loop that ended on its own also passed it (101.0).

No step of any loop stopped: 1633 completed steps over the ten loops, no energy gains, audit failures or slow stretches. Every loop except f* 0.30 and 0.27 reached Gamma 7.0 and was on the way down when cancelled; f* 0.30 was at Gamma 6.7 and 0.27 at 6.0 on the way up. Nothing at width 200 stopped where width 100 did not.

Last completed step of each cancelled loop: f* 0.57 Gamma 2.35 (down, step 199 of 212), 0.50 3.0 (down, 186), 0.44 4.15 (down, 163), 0.38 5.3 (down, 140), 0.33 6.55 (down, 115), 0.30 6.65 (up, 99), 0.27 5.95 (up, 85). Each run folder keeps the latest completed step's checkpoint and checkpoints at Gamma multiples of 0.5, so tools/ramp.py can resume it with the same command.

Matched-step cost ratio width 200 over width 100 (E0060), median: up 9.7 to 11.1 at every f*, down 7.0 to 9.9 (none at 0.30, 0.27). The costliest step per loop is the first (Gamma 1.7), 0.87 to 3.21 CPU-hours, rising as f* falls; no step came near the 4 CPU-hour cap. E0070's short cost holds said 4.7 to 5.6.

The registration's price (34 to 101 CPU-hours a loop) was too low: completed loops cost 80.5, 89.9 and 101.0, and the seven cancelled loops would need, by their width-100 totals (E0060: 11.7 to 25.3 CPU-hours) times their measured up-leg ratio (9.7 to 11.1), roughly 115 to 275 CPU-hours a loop to finish.
Not measured: onset, E0074's registered test. Ring spectra are in the run folders on Hatteras, not mirrored.
